attachments.origin_landmark: lateral surface of the zygomatic bone, in front of zygomaticus major
attachments.insertion_landmark: upper lip lateral to the philtrum

actions: elevates the upper lip, deepening the nasolabial furrow

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Contributes to the sneer, and to exposing the upper teeth in a full smile.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: High-frequency linear probe over the malar cheek, perpendicular to a horizontal line drawn laterally from the lateral canthus (the lateral canthus horizontal plane, LCHP); scanned at the perpendicular plane through the lateral canthus, orbital rim, midpoint of the frontal process of the zygomatic bone, or jugale point.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: The bony-origin fibers of zygomaticus minor lie deep to the inferolateral orbicularis oculi: their superior margin sits 17.9-22.8 mm below the LCHP (varying by reference plane) and a further 3.0-4.5 mm deep to the orbicularis oculi's own inferior margin, which itself lies 4.7-5.5 mm below the skin.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Ask the patient to smile/elevate the upper lip; zygomaticus minor runs medial and roughly parallel to zygomaticus major toward the upper lip rather than the modiolus. In cadaveric dissection its muscle vector runs at a mean of 55.7 degrees from the facial midline, converging with levator labii superioris and levator labii superioris alaeque nasi near a point lateral to the ala (the 'Yonsei point').
structures_at_risk: orbicularis oculi, immediately superficial -- a shared BoNT field with orbicularis oculi (e.g. for crow's feet) risks weakening Zmi and impairing upper-lip elevation if injected too deep or too low
zygomaticus major, running parallel and lateral to Zmi toward the modiolus
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Fibers of orbicularis oculi join zygomaticus minor in a variable proportion of individuals (reported from ~64% up to 100% depending on population studied), so ultrasound depth measurements should be treated as a guide rather than a fixed cutoff when avoiding the zygomaticus complex during orbicularis oculi injections.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Piao JZ, Lee JH, Hu KS, Kim HJ, Clin Anat 39(6):662-671 (2025), doi:10.1002/ca.24290 (https://doi.org/10.1002/ca.24290) -- retrieved via PubMed
